advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm len(str(content)) over-estimation of non-string part content cannot newly refuse a request that fits, given the documented permissive intent.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py:222: `total += len(content) if isinstance(content, str) else len(str(content))`
src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py:207: comment `Deliberately permissive ... so calls that succeed today are not newly refused`
advisory.finding: _request_text_chars stringifies non-string part content with len(str(content)); for structured/multimodal content (e.g. a list UserPromptPart.content or a ToolReturnPart carrying a dict/list) the repr length can be far larger than the true content, over-estimating tokens and potentially refusing a request that would actually fit — contradicting the module's documented 'permissive so calls that succeed today are not newly refused' calibration intent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify msg.instructions and part content are never the same text on the wire, to avoid double-counting the estimate if Agent(instructions=...) is ever adopted.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/runner.py:548: `run_result = agent.run_sync(req.instructions, usage_limits=usage_limits)` — instructions travel as the user prompt part, not the request `instructions` field
advisory.finding: _request_text_chars counts BOTH msg.instructions and every part's content. If a ModelRequest ever carries the instruction text on the `instructions` attribute AND also as a SystemPromptPart/UserPromptPart in `parts` (a plausible pydantic-ai configuration where Agent(instructions=...) is used), the same authoritative text is double-counted, inflating the estimate. Current callers pass instructions as the user prompt positional arg (runner.py:548) so it is not double-counted today, but the coupling is fragile.
